guarantees.claim: mode_q is reset to EntropyModeNone when rst_ni is low.
mode_q is updated with the value of mode_i when mode_latch is high and rst_ni is high.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i, rst_ni high, mode_latch high

guarantees.claim: mode_q holds its previous value on any clock edge where rst_ni is high and mode_latch is low.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i, rst_ni high, mode_latch low

assumptions.claim: mode_i must be a valid EntropyMode enum value whenever mode_latch is asserted.
assumptions.risk: an illegal value in mode_q may cause downstream entropy logic to behave incorrectly, possibly disabling entropy or creating a security weakness.

assumptions.claim: mode_latch must be a clean, glitch-free synchronous pulse (or level) that accurately captures a stable mode_i.
assumptions.risk: a glitch on mode_latch could corrupt mode_q with a transient or invalid mode_i, compromising entropy mode selection.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni must remain low for at least one full clock cycle to ensure the reset value EntropyModeNone is captured.
assumptions.risk: if rst_ni is taken high before the first effective positive clock edge after assertion, mode_q may not be initialized to EntropyModeNone, starting entropy logic in an unknown state.

uncertain_points.claim: The source of mode_latch may be an asynchronous or unsynchronized signal, risking metastable capture of mode_i or multiple unintended updates.
uncertain_points.risk: corruption of mode_q could switch the entropy engine on/off unexpectedly, affecting security by enabling or disabling entropy collection at the wrong time.

uncertain_points.claim: No validation is performed on mode_i before it is captured into mode_q; an illegal value (e.g., reserved encoding) may be blindly stored.
uncertain_points.risk: downstream entropy logic may interpret an invalid mode in a dangerous way (e.g., clearing secret state or entering debug mode) because no guard exists in this chunk.
